title: Symmetric monoidal infinity categories as Segal diagrams
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], enlarging universes as necessary. Let $\mathsf{Fin}_*$ be the category of finite pointed sets, write $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\rho_i:\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ send $i$ to $1$ and every other element to $*$. An inert map has exactly one preimage for each non-basepoint of its target. A Segal diagram is a functor $F:N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)\to\mathsf{Cat}_\infty$ for which $(F(\rho_i))_i:F(\langle n\rangle)\to F(\langle1\rangle)^n$ is an equivalence for every $n\geq0$, including $F(\langle0\rangle)\simeq *$. Here $N$ denotes the simplicial nerve. A symmetric monoidal infinity category is encoded by a cocartesian fibration $p:\mathcal A^{\otimes}\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ whose fiber over $\langle n\rangle$ is identified with $\mathcal A^n$, $\mathcal A=p^{-1}(\langle1\rangle)$, by pushforward along the $\rho_i$. Straightening, which assigns to a cocartesian fibration its fibers and pushforward functors, identifies symmetric monoidal infinity categories with Segal diagrams: the inverse, unstraightening, produces a cocartesian fibration over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ with those fibers. The underlying category is $F(\langle1\rangle)$; the active maps $\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ sending all non-basepoints to $1$ give its $n$-ary tensor operations, including the unit when $n=0$. Natural transformations between Segal diagrams correspond to strong symmetric monoidal functors, meaning functors over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ preserving cocartesian arrows, and this correspondence identifies their spaces of equivalences and higher homotopies.

For symmetric monoidal $\mathcal A^{\otimes},\mathcal B^{\otimes}$, let $\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ be the full infinity subcategory of functors between their total categories over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ spanned by these strong functors; its morphisms are monoidal natural transformations, not necessarily invertible. For every small infinity category $K$, the functor category $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)$ has the pointwise symmetric monoidal structure, classified by $\langle n\rangle\mapsto\operatorname{Fun}(K,F_{\mathcal B}(\langle n\rangle))$, and currying gives a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal A,\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B))\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)).$$
For an ordinary symmetric monoidal category $A$, its operadic nerve $N(A^{\otimes})$ is such a symmetric monoidal infinity category, with underlying category $N(A)$. Here objects of $A^{\otimes}$ are finite tuples, and a morphism over $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$ consists of maps $\bigotimes_{\alpha(i)=j}X_i\to Y_j$ for $1\leq j\leq m$.
